issues.t: Water pump and thermostat housing coolant leak
issues.sym: A sweet coolant smell, pink or purple crust or drips under the front of the engine, a low coolant warning, or the temperature gauge rising. Owners have reported it at under 60,000 miles.
issues.why: On Volkswagen's 2.0L turbo (EA888) engine the water pump and thermostat share a plastic housing that can warp and leak with heat cycles. It is a well-known weak point across VW and Audi models with this engine.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and don't keep driving if the gauge climbs. Have the leak confirmed; the usual fix is a new water pump and thermostat assembly filled with VW-approved coolant. Ask whether any warranty still applies.

issues.t: PCV valve failure causing rough idle
issues.sym: A rough or unsteady idle, a check engine light (often lean codes such as P0171), a whistling or squealing noise from the engine, and sometimes oil smoke from the exhaust.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve on top of the engine has a rubber diaphragm that can tear, or its check valve can stick. That lets unmetered air in and upsets crankcase pressure.
issues.next: Have the PCV valve tested and replaced with the latest version. Don't put it off: high crankcase pressure can push out the rear main seal and cause a bigger oil leak.

issues.sym: The engine shakes or stumbles, especially when accelerating, and the check engine or EPC light comes on, sometimes flashing.
issues.why: Ignition coils on this engine wear out, and worn spark plugs make them work harder. A failed coil stops one cylinder from firing.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Replace the failed coil, and replace the spark plugs too if they are near their interval. Avoid hard driving with a flashing light to protect the catalytic converter.

issues.sym: Oil dripping from where the engine meets the transmission, spots under the middle of the car, and a slowly dropping oil level.
issues.why: The seal at the back of the crankshaft fails more often than it should on this engine generation, and a failing PCV valve can push it out by raising crankcase pressure.
issues.next: Have the leak source confirmed, since oil from higher up can run down to the same spot. The seal itself is a small part, but the transmission has to come out, so it is a big job. Check the PCV valve at the same time.

issues.t: Oil leak from upper timing cover or cam adjuster seal
issues.sym: Oil wetness on the front of the engine near the top timing cover, and a burning-oil smell after driving.
issues.why: The rubber seal on the upper timing cover turns brittle, and the cam bridge/adjuster seal can leak oil into the upper timing cover on this engine generation.
issues.next: Have the leak traced and the seals replaced. Keep an eye on the oil level until it is fixed.

issues.t: Intake manifold flap failure and check engine light
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with an intake manifold runner or flap code. You may notice slightly weaker running or a rough idle.
issues.why: The actuator arm for the flaps inside the intake manifold can break. Volkswagen doesn't sell the small repair parts, so the whole manifold usually has to be replaced.
issues.next: Have the codes read to confirm the flap system is at fault. Ask about aftermarket repair kits, which can be an option instead of a full manifold.

issues.t: Turbo wastegate actuator failure and low power
issues.sym: Noticeably weaker acceleration, a check engine light for boost or turbo control, and sometimes a rattle from the turbo area.
issues.why: The electronic actuator that opens and closes the turbo wastegate is a known failure point on this engine generation, which upsets boost control.
issues.next: Have a shop test the actuator before replacing the whole turbocharger. On some versions the actuator can be replaced on its own for much less.

issues.t: Tire sidewall bubbles and blowouts on 20-inch wheels
issues.sym: A bulge or bubble on a tire sidewall, a sudden flat after hitting a pothole or small bump at low speed, or shaking at highway speeds. Some owners report several blowouts within months.
issues.why: Versions with 20-inch wheels use very low-profile 245/35R20 tires with little sidewall to absorb impacts, so potholes can break the internal cords.
issues.next: Check tire pressure monthly and inspect the sidewalls after hard impacts. Replace any tire with a bubble right away, since it can burst. Consider road hazard coverage, or smaller wheels with taller tires.

issues.t: Infotainment screen lags, freezes or goes black
issues.sym: The touchscreen responds slowly or not at all, Apple CarPlay drops out, the screen goes black, or the map and controls display wrongly. Restarting the car often clears it.
issues.why: Software and electronics faults in the infotainment unit are a common owner complaint on the Arteon, and Volkswagen has issued many electrical service communications for it.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to install the latest infotainment software updates. Note when it happens so the dealer can reproduce it. If the backup camera is affected, check for recalls.

issues.t: Driver assistance warnings and false alerts
issues.sym: Forward collision, lane departure or adaptive cruise warnings flash and beep for no reason, sometimes from the moment you start the car, or the car brakes unexpectedly.
issues.why: Owners have filed complaints with NHTSA about the adaptive cruise, automatic emergency braking and lane keeping systems. Dirty, blocked or misaligned sensors and software faults can cause false alerts.
issues.next: Clean the front radar sensor and windshield camera area. If alerts continue, have the dealer check sensor calibration and software, and note dates and conditions to report.

issues.t: Passenger airbag turned off by seat occupancy sensor
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light stays on with an adult in the seat, along with an airbag warning light or message.
issues.why: The passenger occupant detection system in the seat can misread who is sitting there and switch the passenger airbag off. An owner reported the dealer called it a known issue.
issues.next: Don't let an adult ride in front with the airbag off light on. Have the dealer diagnose the seat sensor; it may be covered by warranty.

issues.sym: An emergency call system error message on the dash, and hands-free phone calling may also stop working.
issues.why: The emergency call (SOS) module can fail. An owner reported the replacement part was back-ordered for nearly a year.
issues.next: Have the dealer diagnose the module and order the part early. Keep your phone handy in the meantime, since automatic crash calling may not work.

issues.t: Weak low-speed pulling power fixed by software update
issues.sym: The car feels sluggish when pulling away or accelerating from low engine speeds.
issues.why: Early Arteons had low torque at low engine speeds, and Volkswagen released a software update to improve it.
issues.next: Ask a VW dealer whether the engine software update has been installed on your car.

issues.t: Brake booster input rod may be installed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels hard and needs more force to stop the car, or braking assist is lost.
issues.why: The pushrod for the electronic brake booster may have been installed incorrectly, which can increase pedal effort or let the rod come loose. Volkswagen recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check the VIN for open recalls. The dealer will inspect and correct the rod or replace the booster for free.

issues.t: Brake booster rod connection can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal goes soft or stops working normally.
issues.why: The connection on the brake booster's pressure input rod may be loose and could separate, which would cause brake pedal failure. Volkswagen recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check the VIN for open recalls right away. The dealer will tighten the connection for free.

issues.t: Tire pressure monitor may miss a low tire (recall)
issues.sym: The tire pressure system may not warn you about a low tire, especially after the tires have been rotated.
issues.why: The tire pressure sensors were calibrated wrong and may lose track of which wheel they are on. Volkswagen recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. The dealer will replace the wheel sensors and valves for free. Check tire pressures by hand until then.

issues.t: Rearview camera goes black or infotainment freezes (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera screen stays black when you shift into reverse, or the infotainment system freezes.
issues.why: A software fault could make the rearview camera malfunction during a drive cycle. Volkswagen recalled affected cars for a software update.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Look over your shoulder and use the mirrors when backing until the update is done.

issues.t: Rearview camera image lost from memory chip fault (recall)
issues.sym: No backup camera image appears on the screen when reversing.
issues.why: A manufacturing problem with the infotainment unit's eMMC memory chip could stop the camera image from showing. Volkswagen recalled several models, including the Arteon, for a software update.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the free software update done.

issues.t: Rearview camera may not display at startup (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera image doesn't show correctly after you start the car and shift into reverse.
issues.why: An error in the camera control unit at startup could stop the rearview image from displaying. Volkswagen recalled affected 2023 Arteons for a camera software update.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Volkswagen said owners would get a second notice when the fix is ready; back up carefully until then.
